key_idea: A figure is just a connected component of the endpoint graph, and it is a polygon exactly when every endpoint in the component has degree 2 (a connected 2-regular graph is a single simple cycle).
sketch: Parse the whole input by extracting every integer and grouping them in fours, ignoring the punctuation and whitespace. Encode a point as 100x+y, union the two endpoints of each segment and count degrees. Count components that contain at least one point, and those whose points all have degree 2. O(S alpha). Pitfalls: the messy input format with arbitrary whitespace and leading blank lines; geometric crossings that are not at endpoints do not connect anything.
